translations.literal: When Zong was junior mentor he once composed a five-hundred-character poem on ascending the palace wall; at the time the heir apparent and Xu Ling and other famous scholars all joined in the same composition.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong was junior mentor he wrote a five-hundred-character poem on climbing the palace wall; the heir apparent, Xu Ling, and other famous scholars all wrote matching pieces.

sentences.zh: 徐公後謂江曰：「我所和弟五十韻，寄弟集內。

translations.literal: Master Xu later told Jiang: "My fifty-rhyme response to my younger brother is in my brother's collection."
translations.idiomatic: Xu later told Jiang, "My fifty-rhyme response to my younger brother is in my brother's collection."

sentences.zh: 」及江編次文章，無復察所和本，述徐此意，謂察曰：「高才碩學，庶光拙文，今須公所和五百字，用偶徐侯章也。

translations.literal: When Jiang arranged his writings he could no longer find Cha's matching piece; stating Xu's meaning, he told Cha: "With lofty talent and great learning you might glorify my poor piece; now I need your five hundred characters to pair with Master Xu's chapter."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang edited his writings he could not find Cha's matching poem; repeating Xu's request, he told Cha, "With your great talent you might glorify my poor piece; I need your five hundred characters to pair with Master Xu's chapter."

sentences.zh: 」察謙遜未付，江曰：「若不得公此制，僕詩亦須棄本，復乖徐公所寄，豈得見令兩失。

translations.literal: Cha modestly did not deliver it; Jiang said: "If I cannot obtain your piece, my poem too must be discarded, and again I fail what Master Xu entrusted—how can both be lost at once?"
translations.idiomatic: Cha modestly withheld it; Jiang said, "Without your piece I must discard my poem too and again fail what Master Xu entrusted—how can both be lost?"

sentences.zh: 」察不獲已，乃寫本付之。

translations.literal: Cha, unable to refuse further, then copied out the piece and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse further, Cha copied out the piece and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 為通人推挹，例皆如此。

translations.literal: Esteemed by men of discernment—every case was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Esteemed by men of discernment—every case was like this.

sentences.zh: 所著漢書訓纂三十卷，說林十卷，西聘、玉璽、建康三鍾等記各一卷，悉窮該博，并文集二十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: His writings include Exegesis and Digest of the Han History in thirty scrolls, Forest of Discourses in ten scrolls, Western Embassy Memorial, Jade Seal Memorial, and Record of the Three Bells of Jiankang, each one scroll—all exhaustively broad—and collected works in twenty scrolls, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Exegesis and Digest of the Han History in thirty scrolls, Forest of Discourses in ten scrolls, and one scroll each on the western embassy, the jade seal, and the three bells of Jiankang—all exhaustively learned—plus collected works in twenty scrolls, all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 察所撰梁、陳史雖未畢功，隋文帝開皇之時，遣內史舍人虞世基索本，且進上，今在內殿。

translations.literal: Though Cha's Liang and Chen histories were not finished, in Emperor Wen of Sui's Kaihuang era the court sent Secretariat Aide Yu Shiji to demand the draft and it was submitted; it is now in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cha's Liang and Chen histories were unfinished, in Sui Wendi's Kaihuang era the court sent secretariat aide Yu Shiji to demand the draft and receive it; it is now in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳二史本多是察之所撰，其中序論及紀、傳有所闕者，臨亡之時，仍以體例誡約子思廉，博訪撰續，思廉泣涕奉行。

translations.literal: The Liang and Chen histories were mostly Cha's composition; prefaces, discussions, annals, and biographies had gaps; on the verge of death he still charged his son Sijian with the format and rules, to seek widely and continue writing; Sijian wept and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang and Chen histories were mostly Cha's work; prefaces, discussions, annals, and biographies still had gaps. On his deathbed he charged his son Sijian with the format and rules to seek sources and continue the work; Sijian wept and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 思廉在陳為衡陽王府法曹參軍，轉會稽王主簿。

translations.literal: Sijian in Chen was recorder in the Hengyang prince's household, then registrar to the prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, Sijian was recorder in the Hengyang prince's household, then registrar to the prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 入隋，補漢王府行參軍，掌記室，尋除河間郡司法。

translations.literal: Entering Sui he was made staff aide to the Prince of Han and director of the secretariat office; soon he was made judicial administrator of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Sui he became staff aide to the prince of Han and director of the secretariat office, then judicial administrator of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 大業初，內史侍郎虞世基奏思廉踵成梁、陳二代史，自爾以來，稍就補續。

translations.literal: At the opening of Daye, Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji memorialized that Sijian should follow and complete the Liang and Chen histories; from then the work gradually was supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Daye, secretariat vice director Yu Shiji memorialized that Sijian should follow and complete the Liang and Chen histories; from then the work was gradually supplemented.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江總持清標簡貴，加潤以辭采，及師長六官，雅允朝望。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Jiang Zong held a clear emblem, simple and noble, adorned with literary color; when he headed the six ministries he fully matched court hopes.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Jiang Zong bore a clear emblem, simple and noble, adorned with literary grace; when he headed the six ministries he fully matched what the court hoped for.

sentences.zh: 史臣先臣稟茲令德，〔一五〕光斯百行，可以厲風俗，可以厚人倫。

translations.literal: The historiographer's late father received these fine virtues [15], illuminating these hundred conduct—he could reform customs and thicken human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer's late father possessed these fine virtues [15] and lit up every side of conduct—he could reform custom and thicken human relations.

sentences.zh: 至於九流、七略之書，名山石室之記，汲郡、孔堂之書，玉箱金板之文，莫不窮研旨奧，遍探坎井，故道冠人師，搢紳以為準的。

translations.literal: As for books of the nine streams and seven summaries, records of famous mountains and stone chambers, books from the Ji commandery and Kong family hall, texts of jade cases and gold boards—none escaped deep study of their purport or full probing of their depths; therefore he led the way as teacher of men, and gentry took him as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Books of the nine streams and seven summaries, records from famous mountains and stone chambers, texts from the Ji cache and Kong hall, writings on jade cases and gold boards—none escaped deep study or full probing; he led the way as a teacher of men, and the gentry took him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 既歷職貴顯，國典朝章，古今疑議，後主皆取先臣斷決焉。

translations.literal: Having served in lofty posts, on state canons and court regulations and ancient and modern doubtful points Houzhu all took my late father's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to lofty posts, on state canons, court regulations, and ancient and modern doubtful points Houzhu always took my late father's judgment.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 舅吳平光侯蕭勱 「勱」梁書蕭景傳、南史吳平侯景傳並作「勵」，南史江總傳又作「勱」。

translations.literal: [1] Uncle Marquis of Pingguang Wu Xiao Mo—"Mo" in the Book of Liang biography of Xiao Jing and the Southern History biography of Marquis of Wu Pingguang Jing both read "Li"; the Southern History biography of Jiang Zong again reads "Mo."
translations.idiomatic: On "uncle Marquis of Pingguang Wu Xiao Mo": the Book of Liang biography of Xiao Jing and the Southern History biography of Marquis of Wu Pingguang Jing read Li for Mo; the Southern History biography of Jiang Zong again reads Mo.

sentences.zh: 按桂馥說文解字義證云「勱」字或作「勵」。

translations.literal: According to Gui Fu's Exegesis of Meaning in the Shuowen, the character "Mo" may also be written "Li."
translations.idiomatic: Gui Fu's Exegesis of Meaning in the Shuowen says Mo may also be written Li.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 侯之王父晉護軍將軍

translations.literal: [2] The marquis's great-grandfather, Jin protector-general of the army
translations.idiomatic: [2] The marquis's great-grandfather, Jin protector-general of the army

translations.literal: (Biao)
translations.idiomatic: (Biao)

sentences.zh: 〔虨〕 按江虨晉書有傳，為江統之子，曾官護軍將軍，今據改。

translations.literal: [Biao]—According to Jiang Biao's biography in the Jin History he was the son of Jiang Tong and once served as protector-general; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Biao]": Jiang Biao has a biography in the Jin History; he was Jiang Tong's son and once served as protector-general; now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 鐫暴秦之

translations.literal: [3] Carved on violent Qin's
translations.idiomatic: [3] Carved on violent Qin's

translations.idiomatic: (at)

sentences.zh: 〔石〕字 殿本考證云「在」字疑誤。

translations.literal: [stone] character—the Hall edition's textual verification says the character "at" is suspected as an error.
translations.idiomatic: On "[stone] character": the Hall edition suspects at is wrong.

sentences.zh: 按此用秦始皇上會稽山，立石刻頌秦德事，「在」當作「石」，形近而訛。

translations.literal: Comment: this uses the First Emperor's ascent of Kuaiji Mountain and erecting a stone inscription praising Qin virtue—"at" should be "stone," a form-similar corruption.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to the First Emperor's ascent of Mount Kuaiji and a stone inscription praising Qin; at should be stone, a form-similar error.

sentences.zh: 文苑英華九七正作「石」，金陵局本已改為「石」，今從之。

translations.literal: Wenyuan yinghua 97 correctly reads "stone"; the Jinling edition already changed it to stone; now followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan yinghua 97 reads stone; the Jinling edition already has stone; now followed.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 雨鳴林而脩颯 「脩」字疑訛，傅增湘校文苑英華，據宋本改作「翛」。

translations.literal: [4] Rain makes the forest sing while wind whistles elegantly—"elegant" is suspected as a corruption; Fu Zengxiang collated Wenyuan yinghua, changing per the Song edition to "whistling."
translations.idiomatic: On "rain makes the forest sing while wind whistles elegantly": elegant is probably corrupt; Fu Zengxiang collated Wenyuan yinghua and, following the Song edition, reads whistling.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 共陳暄孔範王

translations.literal: [5] With Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang
translations.idiomatic: [5] With Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang

translations.idiomatic: (Yuan)

sentences.zh: 〔瑳〕等十餘人 據南史及通鑑陳長城公至德二年改。

translations.literal: [Wang] and more than ten men—changed according to the Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Changcheng Gong Zhide year 2.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Wang] and more than ten men": emended per the Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Changcheng Gong Zhide year 2.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 父上開府僧

translations.literal: [6] Father Director-General of the Upper Secretariat Monk
translations.idiomatic: [6] Father Director-General of the Upper Secretariat Monk

translations.literal: (Tan)
translations.idiomatic: (Tan)

sentences.zh: 〔垣〕 按姚僧垣周書有傳，坦與垣形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: [Yuan]—According to Yao Sengyuan's biography in the Zhou History, tan and yuan are form-similar corruptions; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Yuan]": Yao Sengyuan has a biography in the Zhou History; tan and yuan are form-similar errors; now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: The same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same below.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕 將畢

translations.literal: [7] About to complete
translations.idiomatic: [7] About to complete

translations.literal: (ku)
translations.idiomatic: (ku)

sentences.zh: 〔苫〕壤 據南監本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [ku] mourning shed—changed according to the Southern Supervisory and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[ku] mourning shed": emended per the Southern Supervisory and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 乃神筆草詔 殿本考證云「神」疑「伸」字之誤。

translations.literal: [8] Then with divine brush he drafted the edict—the Hall edition's textual verification says "divine" is suspected as an error for "extend the brush."
translations.idiomatic: On "then with divine brush he drafted the edict": the Hall edition suspects divine for extend the brush.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記云：「古有伸紙，未聞伸筆，『神』字是。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "In antiquity there was extending the paper; extending the brush is unheard of—'divine' is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation note says antiquity had extending the paper, not the brush—divine is correct.

sentences.zh: 」今按文學傳序有「 神筆賞激」語，何之元傳亦有「神筆詔書」語，考證作者竟孰視無睹，淺妄甚矣。

translations.literal: Present examination: the Literary Treatises sequence has the phrase "divine brush reward," and He Zhiyuan's biography also has "divine brush edict"; the author of the verification was utterly blind to these—extremely shallow and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Present examination: the Literary Treatises sequence has divine brush reward, and He Zhiyuan's biography has divine brush edict; the verifier ignored both—shallow and reckless.

sentences.zh: 〔九〕 察垂涕拜請曰臣東皋賤族 「曰臣」二字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: [9] Cha wept and bowed, saying, "I, eastern Gao low clan"—the two characters "said I" were originally ink dots in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "Cha wept and bowed, saying, I, eastern Gao low clan": said I were ink dots in the base text and are restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕花綀一匹 「綀」各本作「練」。

translations.literal: [10] One bolt of patterned silk—"silk" in all editions reads "practice silk."
translations.idiomatic: On "one bolt of patterned silk": all editions read practice silk for silk.

sentences.zh: 按下文云「吾所衣著，止是麻布蒲綀」，蒲綀對花綀而言，作「綀」是，南史正作「綀」。

translations.literal: Comment: below it says "what I wear is only hemp cloth and rush silk"; rush silk pairs with patterned silk, so writing "silk" is correct; the Southern History correctly reads "silk."
translations.idiomatic: Below he says he wears only hemp cloth and rush silk; rush silk pairs with patterned silk, so silk is correct; the Southern History agrees.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕察勵色驅出 「勵」北監本、汲本、殿本作「厲」。

translations.literal: [11] Cha sternly drove him out—"stern" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "fierce."
translations.idiomatic: On "Cha sternly drove him out": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read fierce for stern.

sentences.zh: 按勵厲通。

translations.literal: Comment: stern and fierce are interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and fierce are interchangeable.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕求之於古 「求之於」三字原本墨丁，據元龜一九二補。

translations.literal: [12] Seeking in antiquity—the three characters "seeking in antiquity" were originally ink dots in the base text and are now supplied from Yuan Gui 192.
translations.idiomatic: On "seeking in antiquity": the three words were ink dots in the base text and are restored from Yuan Gui 192.

sentences.zh: 按「求之於古」與下文「在於今世」適相配合，各本作「精當自古」，恐非。

translations.literal: Comment: "seeking in antiquity" pairs with below "in the present age"; various editions read "exquisite since antiquity," which is probably wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking in antiquity pairs with in the present age below; various editions read exquisite since antiquity, which is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕且訪對甚詳明 「甚詳明」三字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: [13] Moreover his responses are very detailed and clear—the three characters "very detailed and clear" were originally ink dots in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "moreover his responses are very detailed and clear": the three words were ink dots in the base text and are restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕上曰我于姚察文章 「上」字、「于」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: [14] The sovereign said, "I toward Yao Cha's essays"—the characters "sovereign" and "toward" were originally ink dots in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "the sovereign said, I toward Yao Cha's essays": sovereign and toward were ink dots in the base text and are restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕史臣先臣稟茲令德 「先」字下之「臣」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: [15] The historiographer's late father received these fine virtues—below "first" the character "minister" was originally an ink dot in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "the historiographer's late father received these fine virtues": below first, minister was an ink dot in the base text and is restored from other editions.
